title: Saving games
key_points: Save game functionality can be complex and may require saving information from multiple objects across multiple levels.
The save function should allow for additional information about an arbitrary number of objects to scale with the complexity of the game.
Identifying persistent objects using groups or other methods is essential before saving game state.
Serialization using JSON or binary formats is necessary to convert object data into a format suitable for storage.
Loading saved game state requires parsing stored data and reconstructing objects and their properties.
limitations: JSON has limitations such as larger file size, limited data types supported, and requirement of custom encoding/decoding logic for complex data structures.
Binary serialization may not include all object properties by default and requires configuring property usage flags in class definition to include them in serialization.
Saving and loading game state can be complicated and often requires custom logic tailored to the specific needs and structure of the project.
asserts: Save games can be implemented using groups to identify persistent objects, with data serialized into JSON or binary format for storage.
scope: The source provides a tutorial on how to implement save game functionality in Godot game engine projects, covering identification of persistent objects, serialization methods, and reconstruction of saved state during load.
